name: RetoSwap
rootCause: RetoSwap (a Tor-based P2P multisig DEX powered by the Haveno trade protocol for trading Monero) was actively exploited. Attackers sent fake, out-of-order ACK messages impersonating the arbitrator during ongoing trades. This tricked the client into updating the arbitrator’s node address to the attacker’s controlled address, allowing them to create a compromised multisig wallet before the victim deposited funds. The exploit mainly affected crypto-to-crypto trades. RetoSwap immediately banned the attacker’s onion address, forced a client version update to halt all trading, and is working on a patch and potential recovery for affected users. Approximately 7,000 XMR were stolen.

descriptions.text: RetoSwap (a Tor-based P2P multisig DEX powered by the Haveno trade protocol for trading Monero) was actively exploited. Attackers sent fake, out-of-order ACK messages impersonating the arbitrator during ongoing trades. This tricked the client into updating the arbitrator’s node address to the attacker’s controlled address, allowing them to create a compromised multisig wallet before the victim deposited funds. The exploit mainly affected crypto-to-crypto trades. RetoSwap immediately banned the attacker’s onion address, forced a client version update to halt all trading, and is working on a patch and potential recovery for affected users. Approximately 7,000 XMR were stolen.

RetoSwap, a decentralized Monero exchange running a Haveno Protocol fork, was exploited for roughly 7,000 XMR (~$2.7 million) on 20 May 2026 when attackers used a forged arbitration message to gain control of multisig wallets and sweep victim funds. The protocol accepted forged arbitration messages without verifying the sender's signature or identity, enabling attackers to impersonate the arbitrator, update the node address, and obtain control during multisig wallet creation.
